Subject: Post-call: encryption & key management — next steps and questionnaire

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Scope we discussed: SOC 2 posture, HIPAA applicability for PHI, encryption in transit & at rest, and options for customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integration.
- HealthLink asked: whether Redwood supports HSM-backed CMKs, what our default KMS is, and whether we can provide a list of evidence artifacts for SOC 2 / encryption controls.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached a simple vendor security questionnaire (HealthLink_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf) — would you mind filling the first page and returning? If you prefer, I can also export our answers into a spreadsheet.
2) Loop in our security engineering for detailed answers on BYOK/HSM options and to prepare the requested artifacts (SOC 2 section 3 evidence, key rotation docs).
3) Suggest a short follow-up call next week (30 min) to run through the questionnaire and confirm the integration pattern for customer-managed keys.

A few quick answers while we wait for our security team:
- At-rest encryption: Yes — all customer data at rest is encrypted. For hosted customers we use cloud KMS with envelope encryption by default.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual auth options for private deployments.
- BYOK: We support customer-managed keys via our Redwood Private deployment and Dedicated options; we can also integrate with customer KMS keys for encryption of model artifacts and blob storage. HSM-backed CMKs are supported when customers require an HSM-backed key in their KMS (e.g., AWS CloudHSM via AWS KMS CMKs).

I’m CCing Marissa from Product so she can help prioritize any integration notes. I’ll also ping security to prepare the SOC 2 artifact list — Rishi, can you take point?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie / Marissa / Alex — quick answers and attachments below. I attached a short "Encryption Evidence Checklist" (redwood-kms-overview-2028-03.pdf) and a one-page BYOK summary. High level: 

1) Hosted + CMK (GCP KMS): We support customer-supplied CMKs for specific storage layers in hosted via per-tenant envelope encryption — this requires minimal configuration (KMS IAM binding and a key policy that allows Redwood's encryption principal to encrypt/decrypt but never export key material). Hosted CMK support is GA for major clouds (GCP, AWS) with the following caveats: you must grant the Redwood service principal a cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role (GCP) and we maintain no capability to extract raw key material.

2) HSM-backed CMKs: Supported where customer's KMS provides HSM-backed keys (e.g., Google Cloud HSM, AWS CloudHSM-backed CMKs). Redwood treats those keys the same as other CMKs; we do not touch key material.

3) SOC 2 / artifacts: Attached checklist maps our SOC 2 encryption controls to the typical questionnaire fields. Artifacts we can provide on request: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), key rotation logs (timestamped), KMS IAM policy snapshots, TLS cert chain for endpoints, and sample configuration showing no-plaintext export paths. Note: some artifact requests will require an NDA or redaction.

4) HIPAA / separation of duties: When BYOK is enabled, key policies can be configured such that Redwood's operational principals have Encrypt/Decrypt permissions only and not key management/export. We can provide an attestation letter for separation-of-duties for enterprise contracts; for PHI workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed HSM for additional assurance.

Next actions:
- Stephanie: propose follow-up time slots (I see availability Tue 3/7 and Wed 3/8).
- Alex: if you can return the first page of the questionnaire today, I'll attach the checklist and SOC 2 pointers in our reply.

Thanks — Rishi
